newsitem.title: USA: Air Force names transport jet after Bob Hope.
newsitem.headline: Air Force names transport jet after Bob Hope.

text.p: The U.S. Air Force said on Tuesday it was naming one of its new C-17 transport jets after entertainer Bob Hope in thanks for his contribution to the service.
It was the latest in a string of military honours over the years for the 93-year-old comedian, who has entertained U.S. troops at home and overseas for more than 50 years.

The dedication ceremony of the 32nd C-17 in its class to be turned over to the Air Force was scheduled to take place later on Tuesday at the McDonnell Douglas Corp. plant in Long Beach, Calif. Hope and his wife, Delores, and Air Force Secretary Sheila Widnall were scheduled to attend.

The four-engined C-17 is designed to land on short runways in battlefield areas with heavy weapons and troops. The aircraft dedicated on Tuesday will be assigned to the Air Force's 437th Airlift Wing at Charleston Air Force Base, South Carolina.
